## A distinct input contract and spatial projection problem

Single-lead ECG reconstruction presents an inherently underdetermined inverse problem: estimating 11 missing lead waveforms from a single observed lead (Lead I **or** Lead II). 

Unlike 3-lead models (which observe Leads I, II, and $V_2$ simultaneously spanning both frontal and transverse planes), a 1-lead model observes only a single 1D projection of the 3D cardiac electrical dipole vector $\mathbf{p}(t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$:
$$V_L(t) = \mathbf{c}_L \cdot \mathbf{p}(t) + \eta_L(t)$$
where $\mathbf{c}_L \in \mathbb{R}^3$ represents the lead vector defined by lead electrode geometry.

## Interactive anatomical lead vector geometry

```{python}
#| label: onelead-anatomical-vectors
# 12-lead standard anatomical coordinates (frontal angle in degrees, transverse angle, radius)
lead_coords = [
    {"lead": "I", "plane": "Frontal", "angle_deg": 0.0, "x": 1.0, "y": 0.0, "z": 0.0, "color": "crimson"},
    {"lead": "II", "plane": "Frontal", "angle_deg": 60.0, "x": 0.5, "y": -0.866, "z": 0.0, "color": "navy"},
    {"lead": "III", "plane": "Frontal", "angle_deg": 120.0, "x": -0.5, "y": -0.866, "z": 0.0, "color": "teal"},
    {"lead": "aVR", "plane": "Frontal", "angle_deg": -150.0, "x": -0.866, "y": 0.5, "z": 0.0, "color": "purple"},
    {"lead": "aVL", "plane": "Frontal", "angle_deg": -30.0, "x": 0.866, "y": 0.5, "z": 0.0, "color": "orange"},
    {"lead": "aVF", "plane": "Frontal", "angle_deg": 90.0, "x": 0.0, "y": -1.0, "z": 0.0, "color": "green"},
    {"lead": "V1", "plane": "Precordial", "angle_deg": 120.0, "x": -0.3, "y": -0.2, "z": 0.9, "color": "royalblue"},
    {"lead": "V2", "plane": "Precordial", "angle_deg": 90.0, "x": 0.0, "y": -0.1, "z": 1.0, "color": "royalblue"},
    {"lead": "V3", "plane": "Precordial", "angle_deg": 60.0, "x": 0.4, "y": -0.2, "z": 0.9, "color": "royalblue"},
    {"lead": "V4", "plane": "Precordial", "angle_deg": 45.0, "x": 0.7, "y": -0.4, "z": 0.6, "color": "royalblue"},
    {"lead": "V5", "plane": "Precordial", "angle_deg": 30.0, "x": 0.9, "y": -0.3, "z": 0.3, "color": "royalblue"},
    {"lead": "V6", "plane": "Precordial", "angle_deg": 0.0, "x": 1.0, "y": 0.0, "z": 0.0, "color": "royalblue"},
]
df_leads = pd.DataFrame(lead_coords)

# 2D Hexaxial Frontal Plane Diagram
fig_hex = go.Figure()
for _, row in df_leads[df_leads["plane"] == "Frontal"].iterrows():
    fig_hex.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[0, row["x"]], y=[0, row["y"]],
        mode="lines+markers+text", name=row["lead"],
        text=["", f"<b>{row['lead']}</b> ({row['angle_deg']:.0f}°)\n"],
        textposition="top center", line=dict(width=3),
        marker=dict(size=[0, 10])
    ))

fig_hex.update_layout(
    title="Hexaxial Frontal Plane Reference System (Einthoven & Goldberger Leads)",
    xaxis=dict(range=[-1.3, 1.3], zeroline=True, showgrid=True),
    yaxis=dict(range=[-1.3, 1.3], zeroline=True, showgrid=True, scaleanchor="x", scaleratio=1),
    height=550, showlegend=True
)
fig_hex.show()

# 3D Thoracic Precordial & Limb Lead Coordinates
fig_3d = go.Figure()
for _, row in df_leads.iterrows():
    fig_3d.add_trace(go.Scatter3d(
        x=[0, row["x"]], y=[0, row["y"]], z=[0, row["z"]],
        mode="lines+markers+text", name=row["lead"],
        text=["", f"{row['lead']}"], textposition="top center",
        line=dict(width=4), marker=dict(size=[0, 6])
    ))

fig_3d.update_layout(
    title="3D Anatomical Lead Vector Projection Geometry (Frontal + Precordial)",
    scene=dict(
        xaxis_title="Right (−) to Left (+)",
        yaxis_title="Superior (+) to Inferior (−)",
        zaxis_title="Posterior (−) to Anterior (+)"
    ),
    height=600
)
fig_3d.show()
```

## Architectural taxonomy and spatial ablation tree

To evaluate whether neural networks can exploit these anatomical projection vectors, ten architectural conditioning variants were systematically formulated:

```{python}
#| label: onelead-arch-taxonomy-table
arch_taxonomy = [
    {"Variant": "a0", "Class": "Baseline", "Description": "Standard 1D UNet autoencoder without spatial conditioning.", "Coordinates": "None", "Modulation": "None", "Rel Params": 1.00},
    {"Variant": "b1_panorama", "Class": "Cylindrical Projection", "Description": "Static learned cylindrical projection embedding.", "Coordinates": "Cylindrical (θ, z)", "Modulation": "Additive", "Rel Params": 1.10},
    {"Variant": "c1_panorama_hybrid", "Class": "Hybrid Embedding", "Description": "Coordinate embedding concatenated with intermediate bottleneck features.", "Coordinates": "Learned + Cylindrical", "Modulation": "Concatenation", "Rel Params": 1.18},
    {"Variant": "d1_panorama_relative", "Class": "Relative Displacement", "Description": "Inter-lead pairwise angular displacement matrix.", "Coordinates": "Pairwise (Δθ, Δz)", "Modulation": "Attention Bias", "Rel Params": 1.15},
    {"Variant": "t000_exact_theta", "Class": "Trigonometric Angle", "Description": "2D fixed angle vectors [cos(θ), sin(θ)].", "Coordinates": "Exact 2D Angles", "Modulation": "Linear Project", "Rel Params": 1.08},
    {"Variant": "t111_exact_theta", "Class": "3D Orientation", "Description": "Full 3D unit orientation vectors [x, y, z].", "Coordinates": "Exact 3D Vectors", "Modulation": "Linear Project", "Rel Params": 1.12},
    {"Variant": "e1_panorama_film", "Class": "FiLM Modulation", "Description": "Feature-wise Linear Modulation: γ(coords) · h + β(coords).", "Coordinates": "True Spherical / Cylindrical", "Modulation": "Affine (Scale + Shift)", "Rel Params": 1.25},
    {"Variant": "pa1_panorama_author", "Class": "Author Baseline", "Description": "Multi-head spatial attention fusion baseline.", "Coordinates": "Author Formulation", "Modulation": "Attention Fusion", "Rel Params": 1.20},
    {"Variant": "cm1_capacity_matched", "Class": "Capacity Control", "Description": "Extra layers matching E1 parameter count but without coordinates.", "Coordinates": "Zero / Dummy", "Modulation": "Dense Layers", "Rel Params": 1.25},
    {"Variant": "pg1_permuted_geometry", "Class": "Falsification Control", "Description": "Scrambled / permuted anatomical lead coordinates.", "Coordinates": "Permuted Scramble", "Modulation": "Affine FiLM", "Rel Params": 1.25},
]
df_arch_tax = pd.DataFrame(arch_taxonomy)
display(df_arch_tax)
```

## Compute overhead versus theoretical parameter complexity

```{python}
#| label: onelead-compute-overhead
fig_comp = px.scatter(
    df_arch_tax, x="Rel Params", y="Variant", color="Class",
    size="Rel Params", text="Modulation",
    labels={"Rel Params": "Relative Parameter Multiplier (x A0 Baseline)", "Variant": "Architectural Variant"},
    title="Parameter Complexity and Modulation Strategies Across Spatial Paradigms"
)
fig_comp.update_traces(textposition="middle right")
fig_comp.update_layout(height=500, xaxis=dict(range=[0.95, 1.35]))
fig_comp.show()
```

## Core mechanism questions and claim hierarchy

1. **A0 $\to$ Spatial Encoding**: Does supplying explicit anatomical coordinates ($\theta, \phi, z$) improve missing-lead estimation over an unconditioned base?
2. **True vs Permuted Geometry ($E_1$ vs $PG_1$)**: Does the network genuinely utilize physiological spatial relationships, or does any arbitrary positional embedding suffice?
3. **Capacity Matching ($E_1$ vs $CM_1$)**: Are observed gains attributable to anatomical conditioning or simply increased parameter capacity?
4. **Generalization & Transport**: Do internal validation advantages persist on external cohorts (RDB)?

The empirical resolutions to these questions are detailed in:
- **Chapter 27**: Comprehensive analysis of internal validation results and learning dynamics across all 60 runs.
- **Chapter 26**: External validation on the 360-record Russian Database (RDB) cohort.
